title: JPMorganChase expands Claude Code to more employees across the firm
summary: JPMorganChase is expanding Claude Code beyond engineering to product, advisors, infrastructure and operations, and security teams. Uses include requirements, risk and controls assessments, incident root cause analysis, and vulnerability fixes. Claude runs in controlled containerized environments without direct employee credentials, with staged access expansion, internal approval for new models, and automated gates that stop Claude from approving its own changes.

title: Claude can design electronic prototypes from start to finish
summary: With Diode Computers, Claude designed three electronic prototypes end to end: a speakerphone, a voice-assistant hub, and a handheld virtual pet. Fable 5.2 scored 69% on an internal board-layout benchmark versus 25% for Fable 5, revising failing designs, writing its own routing tool, and running manufacturability and parts checks. Diode built all three boards from the design files without the usual revision rounds, though the prototypes are early, unvalidated, and were produced without Claude having access to test equipment.

title: The components of agent memory
summary: Anthropic describes 'dreaming,' an offline review of past session transcripts that fixes mistakes, writes notes, and builds memory structures. Memory is layered from raw transcripts and working notes to wikis and a small always-loaded context, and newer Opus 5+ models are better at deciding what to save. In a test across 128 dreaming sessions on a 350k-file corpus, wiki-only answer scores rose from 13% to 48%, suggesting periodic review corrects drift while always-loaded context should stay small.

title: How Curative is building a national provider network with agents on Claude
summary: Curative, a health insurer, built a hierarchy of agents on Claude to negotiate provider contracts, with a lead agent running on Opus. It has signed over 23,000 contracts at roughly 2,000 to 2,400 per week, compared with about 2,100 in all of 2025, and cut claims dispute response times from about 90 days to under 30 minutes. Oversight includes a Haiku judge reviewing every outbound message, a Sonnet rate reviewer, and humans approving uncleared requests.

title: Which Claude model should you build with?
summary: Anthropic published a playbook for choosing among Haiku 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Opus 5.5, and Fable 5.2, covering pricing, effort levels, and subagents. It recommends Opus 5.5 at medium effort as the default, and notes that Fable 5.2 at high effort roughly matched Opus 5.5 at max on FrontierCode 2.0 at about half the cost per task. It also warns that thinking blocks do not carry across tiers and that tool_choice any/tool and budget_tokens settings return 400 errors on some models, so migrations need care.

title: Introducing Claude Whiteboards, Claude Sheets, and Claude Data
summary: Whiteboards and Sheets launch in beta, and Dashboards becomes generally available as Claude Data, all on paid plans. Whiteboards let Claude build timelines, group notes, and draft action items on shared boards with export to doc, deck, Lucid, or Miro, while Sheets creates spreadsheets with formulas and drop-downs, logs each edit, and exports to .xlsx or CSV. Claude Data adds certified metrics, live sharing (beta), caching, and tracked changes with rollback, and on Enterprise, Whiteboards and Sheets are off by default while Claude Data turns on November 19, 2026.
